subject: PE
title: Physical Education 8
description: Eighth-grade physical education that builds on grade 7 by emphasizing team strategy, leadership and the science of exercise. Students compare fitness results to last year, measure skill-related fitness, play new invasion, net, target and striking/fielding games (flag football, team handball, tennis, table tennis, golf, cricket), learn safe resistance training and how body systems adapt, explore social dance and mind-body fitness, compete in multi-part track events, and finish by designing, following and evaluating a two-week personal fitness plan. Sessions work in a yard, park or community center with family or a homeschool group.
framework: California Physical Education Model Content Standards (Grade 8); 2009 CA Physical Education Framework

standards.PE-8.1.1: Demonstrate mature, efficient form in team physical activities by combining and applying movement skills in complex game situations.
standards.PE-8.1.2: Demonstrate offensive, defensive and transition skills (cutting, screening, zone and person-to-person defense) in team invasion games.
standards.PE-8.1.3: Demonstrate advanced striking, serving and volleying skills with implements in net/wall and target games.
standards.PE-8.1.4: Perform social, square and contemporary dances with correct timing, partner etiquette and transitions.
standards.PE-8.1.5: Demonstrate technique in multi-part individual events (hurdles, relays, triple jump) and outdoor/lifetime activities.
standards.PE-8.2.1: Analyze and select offensive and defensive tactics (give-and-go, zone defense, set plays) appropriate to a game situation.
standards.PE-8.2.2: Analyze a movement or skill using biomechanical concepts (levers, angle of release, force absorption, momentum) and give corrective feedback.
standards.PE-8.2.3: Explain how practice schedules, feedback and mental rehearsal improve skill learning.
standards.PE-8.3.1: Participate in moderate-to-vigorous physical activity at least four days each week, including activities outside of class.
standards.PE-8.3.2: Assess health- and skill-related fitness components (agility, balance, coordination, power, reaction time, speed) and interpret results.
standards.PE-8.3.3: Meet Healthy Fitness Zone standards for aerobic capacity, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility and body composition.
standards.PE-8.3.4: Develop, implement and evaluate a two-week personal fitness plan that applies the principles of training.
standards.PE-8.4.1: Explain how the muscular, skeletal, cardiorespiratory and nervous systems respond and adapt to exercise.
standards.PE-8.4.2: Identify major muscle groups and select exercises with safe technique (resistance bands, body weight, light free weights) to strengthen each.
standards.PE-8.4.3: Explain the role of nutrition, hydration and sleep in physical performance and recovery.
standards.PE-8.4.4: Describe how physical activity reduces stress and improves mental and emotional health.
standards.PE-8.5.1: Organize and lead group activities, demonstrating responsible leadership, rules knowledge and etiquette.
standards.PE-8.5.2: Accept responsibility for team success, resolve conflicts respectfully and include others of differing abilities.
standards.PE-8.5.3: Evaluate personal progress toward goals and identify the motivation and barriers that affect lifelong activity.

units.title: Fitness Check-In and Skill-Related Fitness
units.big_idea: Health-related fitness keeps you well; skill-related fitness helps you perform—both can be measured and improved.

units.title: Adventure Challenges and Team Leadership
units.big_idea: Leadership means organizing others, solving problems together and including everyone.

units.title: Invasion Games: Flag Football and Team Handball
units.big_idea: Set plays, transitions and defensive systems turn individual skills into team success.

units.title: Net and Wall Games: Tennis, Table Tennis and Advanced Volleyball
units.big_idea: Spin, placement and team rotations add tactical depth to net games.

units.title: Exercise Science and Resistance Training
units.big_idea: Body systems adapt to training; safe technique, nutrition and sleep make training effective.

units.title: Target and Striking/Fielding Games
units.big_idea: Accuracy depends on consistent mechanics and controlling force and angle.

units.title: Social, Square and Contemporary Dance
units.big_idea: Partner and group dance build rhythm, cooperation and cardiovascular fitness.

units.title: Mind-Body Fitness and Stress Management
units.big_idea: Yoga, breathing and mindful movement build flexibility and reduce stress.

units.title: Track and Field: Multi-Part Events
units.big_idea: Complex events are mastered by breaking them into phases and practicing each.

units.title: Lifetime Activities and Two-Week Fitness Plan
units.big_idea: Choosing activities you enjoy and planning around barriers keeps you active for life.

objectives: Compare results to last year and the Healthy Fitness Zone

days.title: Lead the warm-up
days.work: Lead a family member or sibling through the 10-move dynamic warm-up learned in grade 7, then run 10 minutes of tag-style games.

days.title: PACER re-test
days.work: Complete the 20-meter PACER (or timed mile) and record your score next to last year's.

days.title: Strength re-test
days.work: Complete curl-ups and 90-degree push-ups to cadence and record repetitions.

days.title: Flexibility re-test
days.work: Complete the back-saver sit-and-reach and trunk lift; record both sides.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Graph grade 7 vs. grade 8 scores for each item and write which components improved or declined and why.

weeks.assessment: Completed fitness comparison graph with written analysis.

objectives: Define the six skill-related fitness components
Measure agility, balance, power, reaction time, speed and coordination

days.title: Six components
days.work: Learn the six skill-related components and match each to a sport skill (e.g., power = volleyball spike); do a 20-minute circuit of one drill per component.

days.title: Agility and speed
days.work: Run the Illinois agility course set up with cones and a 40-yard dash; record best of two trials.

days.title: Power
days.work: Measure standing long jump and vertical jump (chalk-on-wall method); record best of three.

days.title: Balance and reaction
days.work: Time a one-leg stork stand with eyes closed and do the ruler-drop reaction test five times; convert drop distance to reaction time.

days.title: Profile
days.work: Create a skill-related fitness profile chart and identify your strongest and weakest component.

objectives: Write SMART goals for one health- and one skill-related component

days.title: Motivation
days.work: Sort a list of reasons people exercise into intrinsic and extrinsic, then list your own top three motivators; finish with a 20-minute jog/walk interval.

days.title: Barriers
days.work: Identify three barriers to being active (time, weather, screens) and write a strategy for each; complete a 15-minute body-weight circuit.

days.title: SMART goals
days.work: Write two SMART goals (one health-related, one skill-related) with a weekly action step for each.

days.title: Activity log
days.work: Begin a 4-day-per-week MVPA log and do a 30-minute activity of your choice outside of class.

days.title: Check
days.work: Share goals with a parent, who signs the goal sheet; play an active game of choice.

weeks.assessment: Signed SMART goal sheet and first week of activity log.

days.title: Tarp flip
days.work: With a group (siblings, co-op), stand on a tarp and flip it over without stepping off; debrief what worked.

days.title: Blind maze
days.work: Guide a blindfolded partner through a cone maze using only verbal directions, then switch roles.

days.title: Helium hoop
days.work: Lower a hula hoop to the ground as a group using only fingertips; try three strategies.

days.title: Raft crossing
days.work: Cross a 10-meter 'river' using only four carpet squares or pool noodles as a group.

days.title: Debrief
days.work: Write a reflection on which communication behaviors helped or hurt the group and one thing you will do differently.

objectives: Plan and lead a warm-up and game
Adapt activities so everyone can participate

days.title: Leadership styles
days.work: Discuss what makes a good coach or team captain; list five leadership behaviors.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Write a 20-minute plan: warm-up, one tag or relay game with rules, and cool-down.

days.title: Modify
days.work: Write two modifications so a younger sibling or someone with limited mobility can play your game fully.

days.title: Lead
days.work: Lead your planned session for family or a homeschool group, explaining rules and safety clearly.

days.title: Evaluate
days.work: Collect a quick thumbs-up/down from participants and self-evaluate your leadership on a rubric.

weeks.assessment: Leadership rubric for the led session.

weeks.topic: Flag football: throwing, catching and routes
objectives: Throw a spiral with correct grip and release

days.title: Spiral grip
days.work: Practice the laces grip, step and follow-through; complete 50 partner throws at 10 yards.

days.title: Catching
days.work: Practice the diamond (above chest) and basket (below chest) catch positions on 40 partner throws.

days.title: Routes
days.work: Run slant, out, post and curl routes against air; partner throws on time.

days.title: Flag pulling
days.work: Practice flag-pulling defense and evasive moves (juke, spin) in a 1-v-1 grid.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Video a partner's throw and identify one biomechanical fix (step foot, elbow height, release point).

weeks.topic: Flag football: plays and game play
objectives: Use zone and person-to-person pass defense

days.title: Draw plays
days.work: Draw three plays (one run, two pass) on a play card with routes for each player.

days.title: Run plays
days.work: Walk through, then run the plays at full speed in 3-v-3 or 2-v-2.

days.title: Defense
days.work: Practice person-to-person and zone coverage and compare which stops short passes better.

days.title: Game
days.work: Play a 5-on-5 or small-sided flag football game with rotating quarterbacks.

days.title: Check
days.work: Self-assess play execution and sportsmanship; take a rules quiz (downs, rushing, scoring).

objectives: Perform the jump shot, bounce pass and three-step rule

days.title: Intro
days.work: Learn team handball's origins and rules (3 seconds, 3 steps, goal area); play a passing keep-away game.

days.title: Passing
days.work: Practice shoulder, bounce and wrist passes on the move in triangle passing drills.

days.title: Shooting
days.work: Practice the step shot and jump shot from outside a taped 6-meter arc at a cone goal.

days.title: Goalkeeping
days.work: Take turns as goalkeeper practicing ready stance and blocking low and high shots.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform a skills check: 10 passes on the move and 5 shots on goal; record results.

weeks.topic: Team handball: transition and game play
objectives: Use a give-and-go and defensive positioning

days.title: Give-and-go
days.work: Practice the give-and-go and the cut to open space in 2-v-1 drills.

days.title: Fast break
days.work: Practice transitioning from defense to a 3-on-2 fast break after a goalkeeper save.

days.title: Screens
days.work: Learn how to set and use a screen to free a shooter.

days.title: Game
days.work: Play a small-sided handball game, rotating positions every 5 minutes.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Write a comparison of strategies in handball, soccer and basketball (all invasion games).

objectives: Apply team strategy in tournament play

days.title: Officiating
days.work: Learn hand signals and common fouls for flag football and handball.

days.title: Tournament day 1
days.work: Play round-robin games; take turns officiating one game.

days.title: Tournament day 2
days.work: Play the second round; your team plans a strategy before each game.

days.title: Finals
days.work: Play championship games and run the scoreboard.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a reflection on teamwork, officiating fairness and how you handled a conflict.

objectives: Perform the forehand and two-hand backhand
Serve overhand into a target box

days.title: Grip and ready
days.work: Learn the eastern forehand grip and ready position; rally against a wall for 10 minutes.

days.title: Forehand
days.work: Practice drop-and-hit forehands, focusing on low-to-high swing for topspin.

days.title: Backhand
days.work: Practice the two-hand backhand from a partner toss.

days.title: Serve
days.work: Practice the overhand serve with the 'trophy' position into a chalked target box.

days.title: Check
days.work: Self-video a forehand and compare it to a skill checklist (turn, contact point, follow-through).

weeks.topic: Tennis and table tennis: rallies and scoring
objectives: Keep score in tennis and table tennis

days.title: Tennis rallies
days.work: Rally cooperatively with a partner aiming for 10 consecutive hits.

days.title: Tennis scoring
days.work: Learn love-15-30-40-deuce scoring and play a tiebreaker game.

days.title: Table tennis
days.work: Learn the shakehand grip, push and forehand drive on a table or improvised surface.

days.title: Spin
days.work: Experiment with topspin and backspin in table tennis and describe how the ball reacts.

days.title: Mini-match
days.work: Play a best-of-three table tennis match to 11 and a short tennis set.

weeks.assessment: Scoring quiz and match play observation.

weeks.topic: Advanced volleyball: spike, block and rotation

days.title: Review
days.work: Review grade 7 forearm pass and set with 50 partner contacts each.

days.title: Approach
days.work: Learn the 3-step spike approach (left-right-left) and arm swing using a tossed ball.

days.title: Block
days.work: Practice the two-hand block footwork and timing at the net.

days.title: Rotation
days.work: Learn 6-player rotation and practice pass-set-hit sequences in small groups.

days.title: Game
days.work: Play a modified game requiring three contacts before returning the ball.

days.title: Practice types
days.work: Learn blocked vs. random practice; do 10 minutes of each with tennis forehands and note the difference.

days.title: Mental rehearsal
days.work: Visualize a serve for 2 minutes before 20 serves and compare accuracy to 20 serves without it.

days.title: Peer coaching
days.work: Coach a partner on one net-game skill using a 'praise-fix-praise' feedback format.

days.title: Choice tournament
days.work: Play a mini-tournament in the net game of your choice.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a written test on net-game strategy, scoring and practice principles.

days.title: Short-term responses
days.work: Record heart rate, breathing rate and skin temperature at rest, after 5 minutes of jogging, and after 5 minutes of rest.

days.title: Cardiorespiratory
days.work: Learn how stroke volume and cardiac output increase with training; do a 25-minute interval run.

days.title: Muscles and bones
days.work: Explain how resistance exercise builds muscle and bone density; do a plyometric circuit (jumps, skips).

days.title: Nervous system
days.work: Explain how practice builds neuromuscular coordination; do a 15-minute footwork ladder drill.

days.title: Check
days.work: Create a diagram showing how four body systems respond and adapt to exercise.

weeks.topic: Major muscles and safe resistance training

days.title: Muscle map
days.work: Label a muscle chart with 10 major muscles and one exercise for each.

days.title: Lower body
days.work: Learn proper squat, lunge and glute bridge form; do 3 sets of 10-12 reps.

days.title: Upper body
days.work: Learn push-up, band row and overhead press technique; do 3 sets of 10-12 reps.

days.title: Core
days.work: Learn plank, side plank, bird dog and dead bug; hold or repeat for 3 rounds.

days.title: Check
days.work: Demonstrate six exercises with correct form while a parent uses a technique checklist.

objectives: Apply sets, reps and rest for muscular endurance vs. strength

days.title: Endurance vs. strength
days.work: Compare rep ranges and rest periods for endurance and strength; do an endurance circuit (15-20 reps).

days.title: Balance
days.work: Plan a full-body workout that pairs opposing muscles (chest/back, quads/hamstrings).

days.title: Try it
days.work: Complete your designed workout and record sets, reps and perceived exertion.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Adjust exercises that felt too easy or hard using the progression principle.

days.title: Check
days.work: Submit your workout plan with rationale for each exercise.

weeks.topic: Fueling performance: nutrition, hydration and sleep
objectives: Explain hydration and sleep's role in recovery

days.title: Pre-exercise fuel
days.work: Plan three pre-workout snacks and explain why carbohydrates are the main fuel; do a 30-minute activity.

days.title: Hydration
days.work: Weigh yourself before and after a 30-minute workout to estimate sweat loss and calculate fluid needs.

days.title: Recovery
days.work: Plan a post-workout snack with protein and carbohydrates and explain muscle repair.

days.title: Sleep
days.work: Log sleep for the week and compare to the 8-10 hours recommended for teens; do a yoga cool-down.

days.title: Check
days.work: Create a one-day 'athlete's fuel plan' poster.

weeks.topic: Semester fitness check and plan revision

days.title: Mid-year re-test
days.work: Retest the two fitness items tied to your SMART goals.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Compare results with week 1 and identify whether you progressed, plateaued or declined.

days.title: Overtraining
days.work: Learn signs of overtraining and injury (persistent soreness, fatigue) and how rest prevents them.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise your SMART goals and weekly activity plan for semester 2.

days.title: Active day
days.work: Complete a 40-minute activity of your choice combining cardio and strength.

weeks.assessment: Revised goals and mid-year progress report.

objectives: Perform a golf putt, chip and short swing
Throw backhand and forehand disc golf drives
materials: plastic golf balls or whiffle balls

days.title: Putting
days.work: Practice the putting grip and pendulum stroke to a cup or target from 3, 6 and 9 feet.

days.title: Chipping
days.work: Practice chipping whiffle balls into a hula hoop from 10 and 20 feet.

days.title: Disc drive
days.work: Practice the backhand drive with reach-back and follow-through; measure distances.

days.title: Course
days.work: Set up a 6-hole disc golf or backyard golf course and play a round, keeping score relative to par.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Explain how angle of release and follow-through affected your distance and accuracy.

days.title: Bocce/bean bag
days.work: Play bocce-style target toss, using underhand toss and controlled force.

days.title: Bowling
days.work: Bowl a playground ball at 10 plastic-bottle pins; learn approach and release.

days.title: Target throw
days.work: Throw at a three-ring target from three distances and record scores.

days.title: Routine
days.work: Design a personal pre-shot routine and compare scores with and without it.

days.title: Check
days.work: Compete in a target-skills triathlon (bowling, bocce, target throw) and record totals.

days.title: Cricket intro
days.work: Learn cricket's basic rules and bowl a straight-arm underhand-to-overhand delivery.

days.title: Cricket batting
days.work: Practice defensive and drive strokes to protect the wicket.

days.title: Fielding
days.work: Practice fielding positions and backing up in kickball and cricket.

days.title: Game
days.work: Play a modified cricket or kickball game, rotating batting order.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare strategy in cricket, softball and kickball (striking/fielding games).

objectives: Design an original game with rules and safety

days.title: Design
days.work: Design a game combining elements of two game categories (e.g., target + invasion); write rules and scoring.

days.title: Safety
days.work: Add safety rules and equipment checks; draw the playing area.

days.title: Test
days.work: Play-test with family or friends and note problems.

days.title: Refine
days.work: Revise rules based on the play-test and add a modification for younger players.

days.title: Present
days.work: Teach and play the final version; submit the written rules.

weeks.assessment: Written game rules and teaching session.

days.title: Basic calls
days.work: Learn honor your partner, do-si-do, swing and promenade.

days.title: Squares
days.work: Practice a simple square dance with family or a group of four to eight.

days.title: Calling
days.work: Take a turn as caller, giving clear calls on the beat.

days.title: Folk dance
days.work: Learn a Mexican folk dance step (e.g., zapateado basic) or the Virginia reel.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform a full square dance; self-assess timing and etiquette.

days.title: Rhythm
days.work: Count beats in different songs and clap the tempo; march to 8-counts.

days.title: Swing
days.work: Learn the East Coast swing basic and an underarm turn.

days.title: Salsa
days.work: Learn the salsa basic and cross-body lead.

days.title: Intensity
days.work: Dance 15 minutes continuously and measure heart rate to check if it is MVPA.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform a 1-minute partner routine combining steps.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Choose a song and map out 4 sections of 8-counts with fitness moves (jumps, squats, kicks).

days.title: Choreograph
days.work: Create transitions and formations for a small group.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse and adjust intensity so all participants can join.

days.title: Lead
days.work: Lead family or friends through your dance-fitness routine.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write how dance builds fitness and community; record heart rate during the routine.

days.title: Sun salutation
days.work: Learn and perform a sun salutation sequence five times.

days.title: Balance poses
days.work: Practice tree, warrior III and chair pose; hold each 30 seconds.

days.title: PNF stretching
days.work: Learn contract-relax PNF hamstring stretching with a strap and measure sit-and-reach before and after.

days.title: Flow
days.work: Create a 15-minute yoga flow of 10 poses.

days.title: Check
days.work: Lead your flow for a family member and record flexibility progress.

weeks.assessment: Yoga flow sequence and flexibility measurement.

days.title: Stress and exercise
days.work: Learn how endorphins and reduced cortisol help mood; rate your mood before and after a 20-minute run.

days.title: Breathing
days.work: Practice box breathing and diaphragmatic breathing, then a 10-minute walk.

days.title: Tai chi
days.work: Follow a beginner tai chi sequence for 15 minutes.

days.title: Mindful walk
days.work: Take a 30-minute mindful nature walk, noting five things you see, hear and feel.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a personal stress-relief activity plan with three activities.

objectives: Perform a blind relay baton exchange
Clear low hurdles with correct lead leg

days.title: Baton exchange
days.work: Practice the upsweep and downsweep handoff while jogging, then at speed.

days.title: Relay
days.work: Run a 4 x 100 m relay (or shuttle relay) with a team, staying in the exchange zone.

days.title: Hurdle drills
days.work: Practice lead-leg and trail-leg drills walking beside low pool-noodle hurdles.

days.title: Hurdle runs
days.work: Run a 3-step rhythm over three low hurdles and time it.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Video a hurdle clearance and identify one technique fix.

weeks.topic: Jumps and throws: triple jump and shot technique
objectives: Use the glide or standing put with a soft ball

days.title: Triple jump phases
days.work: Practice hop-step-jump from a standing start, then with a short approach.

days.title: Triple jump measure
days.work: Take three measured jumps and record the best.

days.title: Standing put
days.work: Practice the standing put with a softball or light medicine ball, pushing not throwing.

days.title: Optimal angle
days.work: Test release angles of about 30, 40 and 50 degrees and record distances.

days.title: Check
days.work: Explain how momentum transfers through each phase of the triple jump.

weeks.assessment: Triple jump and put distance log with explanation.

objectives: Compete in a family/co-op track meet
Use even pacing in the 800 m

days.title: Pacing
days.work: Run 4 x 200 m at goal 800 m pace with rest, checking split times.

days.title: Meet plan
days.work: Choose three events and set a goal for each.

days.title: Meet day 1
days.work: Compete in sprint and relay events.

days.title: Meet day 2
days.work: Compete in the 800 m, triple jump and put; record results.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Compare results to goals and grade 7 marks; write a personal-record reflection.

weeks.topic: Lifetime activities: cycling, hiking and swimming safety

days.title: Bike safety
days.work: Do a helmet fit and ABC bike check and practice hand signals on a quiet street.

days.title: Ride
days.work: Ride a planned 30- to 60-minute route with a parent.

days.title: Water safety
days.work: Learn water safety rules and, if available, swim 10 minutes at a local pool.

days.title: Hike
days.work: Plan and complete a hike with a map, water and Leave No Trace principles.

days.title: Community
days.work: List five free or low-cost recreation programs in your community.

weeks.assessment: Outing plan and community recreation list.

days.title: Aerobic test
days.work: Complete the PACER or mile and record.

days.title: Strength tests
days.work: Complete curl-ups and push-ups to cadence.

days.title: Flexibility tests
days.work: Complete sit-and-reach and trunk lift.

days.title: Skill-related tests
days.work: Retest agility, power and reaction time from week 2.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Graph week 1, mid-year and final results and write a progress summary.

weeks.assessment: Year-long fitness progress graph and summary.

objectives: Write a two-week plan using FITT and training principles

days.title: Plan structure
days.work: Outline 14 days with cardio, strength, flexibility and rest days using FITT for each.

days.title: Activity choice
days.work: Choose enjoyable activities from this year's units and justify them.

days.title: Barriers
days.work: Add backup plans for bad weather, busy days or no equipment.

days.title: Start
days.work: Begin day 1 of your plan and log it.

days.title: Review
days.work: Have a parent review the plan for safety and balance; revise if needed.

days.title: Plan day
days.work: Complete the scheduled workout and log heart rate and perceived exertion.

days.title: Plan day
days.work: Complete the scheduled strength and flexibility workout.

days.title: Plan day
days.work: Complete the scheduled cardio workout, recording time and intensity.

days.title: Plan day
days.work: Complete the scheduled activity or active rest day.

days.title: Mid-plan check
days.work: Calculate adherence so far and adjust next week's plan if needed.

weeks.topic: Plan evaluation and transition to high school PE
objectives: Set goals for high school PE

days.title: Plan day
days.work: Complete the scheduled workout and log it.

days.title: Plan day
days.work: Complete the final scheduled workout of the two weeks.

days.title: Evaluate
days.work: Write an evaluation of your plan: adherence, enjoyment and results, plus one change.

days.title: Looking ahead
days.work: Research high school PE course requirements and write two goals for grade 9.

days.title: Field day
days.work: Organize and lead a family or co-op field day with stations from this year's units.

weeks.assessment: Plan evaluation and field day leadership.
